learning_outcomes.text: Explains the structure of the atom, properties of matter, and fundamental concepts of chemistry.
Correctly applies the naming of compounds, formula writing, and calculations.
Analyzes the periodic system and electron configurations of atoms.
Understands types of chemical bonds and fundamental laws of chemistry.
Performs calculations for atomic and molecular masses, the mole concept, and composition.
Applies gas laws, thermochemistry, and thermodynamic principles to problem-solving.
Explains and exemplifies electrochemistry, corrosion, and acid-base theories.
Applies scientific analysis and problem-solving methods to chemical problems.
Relates chemical knowledge to engineering and industrial examples.
Acquires teamwork, research, and reporting skills through project work.

syllabus_topics: SI International Unit System; Number rounding; Structure of matter; Quantum theory
General properties of substances; Distinguishing properties of substances; Separation of mixtures; Decomposition of compounds; Physical and Chemical changes
Atomic structure; Atomic models; Applications; Periodic relationships between elements
Periodic system and electron configurations of atoms; Applications
General properties of gases; Boyle's Law; Charles's Law; Avogadro's Law; Ideal gas law and gas mixtures
Thermochemistry; Concepts of energy, work, heat, and enthalpy; Endothermic and exothermic reactions; Enthalpy change and Hess's law
Electrochemistry; Concepts of oxidation and reduction; Electrochemical cells, electrolysis, and batteries
Galvanic (Voltaic) Cells; Thermodynamics of Electrochemical Cells
Corrosion; Corrosion Mechanism; Prevention of Corrosion
Effects of corrosion on engineering applications, corrosion calculations in material selection, and anti-corrosion coating techniques
Acids and Bases; Acid-base theories (Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry, Lewis); Properties and reactions of acids and bases; pH, pOH calculations, weak acid and base equilibrium
